stages.name: trigger
stages.what: push to main or a pull_request event starts the workflow.
stages.why: Every change gets the same gates, whether or not a human remembers to run them.
stages.failures: A branch nobody pushes to a PR never gets checked.

stages.name: runner
stages.what: GitHub provisions a fresh ubuntu-latest VM (GitLab: python:3.12-bookworm container) with timeout-minutes: 10.
stages.why: A clean machine proves the repo is self-contained — nothing works 'because of my laptop'.
stages.failures: Dependencies not declared in pyproject.toml fail here even though they pass locally.

stages.name: install
stages.what: pip install -e '.[dev,cpp]' with pip caching, plus apt-get install gdb.
stages.why: The editable install is exactly what a new contributor does — CI tests the onboarding path too. The cpp extra brings CMake and Ninja from PyPI so the build system is pinned per checkout.
stages.failures: A stale cache is a rare but real source of 'works locally, red in CI'.

stages.name: native build
stages.what: cmake -S cpp -B cpp/build, cmake --build, then ctest -C Debug --output-junit into evidence/junit/.
stages.why: The C++ DUT is a second implementation of the same protocol, so it has to be built and unit-tested before anything drives it. On GitLab this is a separate `native` stage that installs its own compiler.
stages.source: .github/workflows/ci.yml (Build the C++ DUT / Run CTest); .gitlab-ci.yml (native stage)
stages.failures: A compiler present locally but absent on the runner turns a green desk into a red pipeline — which is the point of running it here.

stages.name: quality gates
stages.what: ruff check → ruff format --check → mypy → pytest → the protocol suite again with --dut cpp, each exiting nonzero on failure.
stages.why: The runner sees only exit codes; every tool's exit status is a contract. The final run proves the requirement tests hold against the native DUT too, not just the Python one.
stages.source: .github/workflows/ci.yml (Lint/Type check/Run tests/Run the protocol suite against the C++ DUT)
stages.failures: Piping a command can hide its exit code — the pipeline's truth is the step's exit status.

stages.name: artifacts
stages.what: upload-artifact with if: always() ships evidence/ (JUnit, DUT log, coverage) even when a step failed.
stages.why: Failures are exactly when you need the logs. always() is the difference between diagnosable and guesswork.
stages.failures: if-no-files-found: error turns 'evidence silently missing' into a loud failure.
